principles.title: Build a balanced plate
principles.body: About half vegetables and fruit, a quarter protein, and a quarter grains or starchy foods (whole grains when your stomach is comfortable with them), plus a little healthy fat.

principles.title: Include protein at every meal
principles.body: It keeps you full and supports muscles: dal, beans, paneer, tofu, curd/yoghurt, eggs, fish, chicken, nuts and seeds.

principles.title: Choose mostly whole, minimally processed foods
principles.body: Cook at home when you can.

principles.title: Go easy on added sugar
principles.body: Fewer sweets, sugary drinks and packaged snacks. Fruit is the better sweet.

principles.title: Go easy on salt and deep-fried food
principles.body: Flavour with herbs, spices, lemon, garlic and ginger instead.

principles.title: Use healthy fats in moderation
principles.body: Nuts, seeds, avocado, and oils like mustard, groundnut or olive oil, rather than lots of butter, ghee or vanaspati.

principles.title: Drink water through the day
principles.body: Let thirst and pale-yellow urine guide you. Plain water, buttermilk (chaas), unsweetened tea or infused water rather than sugary drinks.

principles.title: Eat regularly and mindfully
principles.body: Sit down, slow down and stop when comfortably full.

gentleGuidance.title: Gentle on the stomach
gentleGuidance.body:
Gentle meals use foods that are easier to digest: well-cooked, peeled and soft vegetables, refined grains like white rice, and lean proteins.

A low-fibre diet is usually meant to be **short-term or guided by your doctor**. Fibre is important for long-term gut and heart health. When you feel better, try adding fibre back slowly, one food at a time, in small amounts.

**See a doctor if** you have stomach pain that doesn't go away, blood in your stool, black stools, unexplained weight loss, vomiting, diarrhoea lasting more than a few days, difficulty swallowing, or symptoms that wake you at night.

meals.title: Vegetable oats upma with peanuts
ingredients: 1/2 cup chopped carrot, peas and beans
steps: Dry-roast the oats for 2 minutes and set aside.
Heat the oil, splutter the mustard seeds and curry leaves, then cook the vegetables with a splash of water until tender.
Add the oats and 3/4 cup water. Stir for 2–3 minutes until soft.
Finish with peanuts, salt and a squeeze of lemon.
meals.tip: Make a double batch of the vegetable base and add oats fresh each morning.

meals.title: Moong dal chilla with mint chutney and curd
ingredients: 1/2 cup split moong dal, soaked 3 hours
steps: Grind the soaked dal with a little water, ginger and chilli into a smooth batter.
Spread a ladle of batter thinly on a hot non-stick pan.
Cook with a few drops of oil until golden on both sides.
Serve with mint chutney and curd.
meals.tip: Soak the dal the night before so the batter takes two minutes.

meals.title: Besan chilla with grated vegetables
steps: Whisk the besan with water into a pourable batter and stir in the spices.
Fold in the grated vegetables and coriander.
Pour onto a hot greased pan and spread out.
Cook both sides until golden and serve hot.
meals.tip: Let the batter rest 10 minutes for softer chillas.

meals.title: Overnight oats with milk, chia seeds and berries
ingredients: Handful of berries or chopped fruit
steps: Mix oats, milk and chia seeds in a jar and stir well.
Refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
In the morning, stir and top with the fruit.
Add a little honey only if you like it sweeter.
meals.tip: Add a spoon of curd or nut butter for extra protein.

meals.title: Ragi porridge with nuts and banana
steps: Mix the ragi flour with a little cold water to a smooth paste.
Heat the milk, stir in the paste and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick.
Add cardamom and pour into a bowl.
Top with banana and nuts.
meals.tip: Stir without stopping at first to avoid lumps.

meals.title: Poha with peas, peanuts and lemon, plus a glass of milk or curd
ingredients: 1 tsp oil, mustard seeds, curry leaves
steps: Rinse the poha in a sieve until just soft, and drain well.
Heat the oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, peanuts and peas, and cook until the peas are tender.
Add turmeric, salt and the poha. Toss gently for 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and serve with milk or curd.
meals.tip: Don't soak the poha. Rinsing is enough, or it turns mushy.

meals.title: Whole-grain toast with peanut butter and banana
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread with peanut butter.
Top with banana slices and a pinch of cinnamon.
meals.tip: Choose peanut butter with just peanuts and salt on the label.

meals.title: Greek yoghurt or hung curd with fruit, nuts and seeds
ingredients: 3/4 cup Greek yoghurt or hung curd
steps: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl.
Add the fruit.
Sprinkle over nuts and seeds.
meals.tip: To make hung curd, tie curd in a clean cloth and hang for 2 hours.

meals.title: Sprouts salad with tomato, onion and lemon
steps: Steam the sprouts for 5 minutes, or use them raw if you're used to them.
Mix with the tomato, onion, coriander and chilli.
Season with lemon juice, chaat masala and salt.
meals.tip: Steaming makes sprouts easier to digest.

meals.title: Vegetable omelette with whole-grain toast
ingredients: 1/4 cup chopped onion, tomato and capsicum
steps: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and stir in the vegetables.
Pour into a hot greased pan.
Cook on medium heat until set, then fold and flip once.
Serve with the toast.
meals.tip: A splash of milk makes the omelette fluffier.

meals.title: Two boiled eggs, a fruit and a handful of nuts
steps: Place the eggs in boiling water and cook for 9–10 minutes.
Cool in cold water, then peel.
Serve with the fruit and nuts.
meals.tip: Boil a batch on Sunday and keep them in the fridge for up to 5 days.

meals.title: Tofu scramble with spinach and whole-grain toast
steps: Crumble the tofu with your hands.
Heat the oil, add cumin and the tofu with turmeric and salt, and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Serve with the toast.
meals.tip: Press the tofu in a clean cloth first so the scramble isn't watery.

meals.title: Smoked fish or chicken with whole-grain toast and tomato
ingredients: 60–80 g smoked fish or cooked chicken
steps: Toast the bread.
Top with tomato slices and the fish or chicken.
Finish with pepper and a squeeze of lemon.
meals.tip: Pick smoked fish with less salt where you can.

meals.title: 2 whole-wheat rotis + dal + seasonal sabzi + salad + curd
steps: Cook the dal with turmeric and salt, then add a tempering of cumin and garlic.
Cook the sabzi with minimal oil and spices.
Make fresh rotis.
Plate with salad and curd.
meals.tip: Make the dal in a pressure cooker and the sabzi at the same time to save time.

meals.title: Brown rice or millet + rajma or chole + cucumber raita
ingredients: 1 cup cooked brown rice or millet
steps: Cook the rajma or chole with an onion-tomato masala until thick.
Cook the rice or millet.
Mix curd, cucumber and roasted cumin for the raita.
Serve together.
meals.tip: Soak beans overnight and cook them until completely soft.

meals.title: Quinoa or millet pulao with vegetables + dal
steps: Heat the oil and add whole spices and the vegetables.
Add the grain and 1 cup of water, then cook covered until fluffy.
Warm the dal.
Serve the pulao with the dal.
meals.tip: Rinse quinoa well to remove its bitter coating.

meals.title: Paneer bhurji wrap in a whole-wheat roti with salad
ingredients: 1/4 cup chopped onion, tomato and capsicum
steps: Cook the onion, tomato and capsicum with the spices for 3 minutes.
Add the paneer and cook for 2 more minutes.
Spoon the bhurji onto the roti, add salad and roll up.
meals.tip: Wrap in foil or paper to take it to work.

meals.title: Tofu and vegetable stir-fry with brown rice
steps: Pan-fry the tofu until lightly golden and set aside.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger and vegetables on high heat for 4–5 minutes.
Add the tofu, a splash of soy sauce and pepper.
Serve over the rice.
meals.tip: Keep the vegetables a little crunchy so they hold their nutrients.

meals.title: Egg curry + roti + sautéed greens
ingredients: Turmeric, chilli, coriander powder, 1 tsp oil
steps: Cook the onion, ginger-garlic and tomato with the spices into a thick masala.
Add 1/2 cup water and the halved eggs, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Sauté the greens with garlic.
Serve with rotis.
meals.tip: Score the eggs lightly so the masala soaks in.

meals.title: Grilled chicken or fish + brown rice + vegetables
ingredients: 120 g chicken breast or fish fillet
Lemon, garlic, pepper, a little oil
steps: Marinate the chicken or fish in lemon, garlic, pepper and salt for 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-cook until done (chicken to 75°C inside).
Steam the vegetables.
Plate with the rice.
meals.tip: Don't overcook fish. It's done when it flakes easily.

meals.title: Lentil soup + whole-grain bread + big salad
steps: Cook the lentils with the chopped vegetables and spices until very soft.
Mash lightly or blend if you like it smooth.
Add lemon juice.
Serve with bread and the salad.
meals.tip: Freeze portions of the soup for busy days.

meals.title: Vegetable khichdi (brown rice or millet + moong dal) with curd
ingredients: Turmeric, cumin, ginger, salt, 1 tsp ghee or oil
steps: Rinse the rice and dal together.
Pressure-cook with the vegetables, spices and about 2.5 cups of water until very soft.
Finish with a little ghee or oil.
Serve warm with curd.
meals.tip: Add extra water for a softer, soupier khichdi.

meals.title: Mixed-vegetable soup + paneer tikka
steps: Simmer the vegetables with onion, garlic and water until soft, then blend if you like.
Marinate the paneer in curd, spices and lemon for 15 minutes.
Pan-grill the paneer until golden.
Serve the soup with the paneer.
meals.tip: Thread paneer and capsicum on skewers for a nicer tikka.

meals.title: Dal + 1–2 rotis + stir-fried vegetables
steps: Cook the dal with turmeric and add a garlic-cumin tempering.
Stir-fry the vegetables in a little oil for 5–6 minutes.
Make the rotis.
Serve together.
meals.tip: Keep dinner light and finish 2–3 hours before bed.

meals.title: Chickpea and vegetable curry with a small portion of rice
steps: Make a masala from the onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices.
Add the chickpeas, vegetables and a cup of water.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Serve with the rice.
meals.tip: Mash a few chickpeas into the gravy to thicken it naturally.

meals.title: Egg bhurji + roti + salad
steps: Sauté the onion, chilli and tomato.
Pour in the beaten eggs with turmeric and salt.
Stir until just set.
Serve with rotis and salad.
meals.tip: Take it off the heat while still slightly moist. It keeps cooking.

meals.title: Fish curry or grilled fish + vegetables + small rice portion
ingredients: Onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, spices, 1 tsp oil (for curry)
Or lemon, pepper and a little oil (for grilled)
steps: For curry: make a light masala, add water and the fish pieces, and simmer 8–10 minutes.
For grilled: marinate in lemon and pepper, then grill 4–5 minutes per side.
Steam or stir-fry the vegetables.
Serve with a small portion of rice.
meals.tip: Avoid stirring the curry too much so the fish doesn't break.

meals.title: Chicken and vegetable soup with whole-grain bread
steps: Simmer the chicken with garlic, ginger and water for 15 minutes.
Add the vegetables and cook until tender.
Shred the chicken and return it to the pot.
Season and serve with bread.
meals.tip: Make the broth ahead and freeze it in portions.

meals.title: Fruit + a handful of nuts
ingredients: A small handful of nuts (about 10 almonds)
steps: Wash and slice the fruit.
Eat with the nuts.
meals.tip: Keep the portion small. Nuts are filling and calorie-dense.

meals.title: Roasted chana or makhana
ingredients: 1/4 cup roasted chana or makhana (fox nuts)
Pinch of salt, pepper or chaat masala
steps: If using makhana, dry-roast for 5–6 minutes until crisp.
Toss with a pinch of salt and your spice.
meals.tip: Makhana is lighter and easier on the stomach than roasted chana.

meals.title: Sprouts chaat
steps: Mix the sprouts with the chopped vegetables.
Add lemon, chaat masala and coriander.
Serve right away.
meals.tip: Steam the sprouts for 5 minutes if raw ones upset you.

meals.title: Buttermilk (chaas) or a small bowl of curd
ingredients: Roasted cumin, salt, mint or coriander
steps: Whisk the curd with the water until smooth.
Add roasted cumin, salt and mint.
Serve cold.
meals.tip: A great afternoon drink in place of a sugary one.

meals.title: Hummus with carrot and cucumber sticks
ingredients: Lemon juice, garlic, salt, a little water
steps: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic and salt with a splash of water until smooth.
Cut the vegetables into sticks.
Dip and enjoy.
meals.tip: Add more water or olive oil to loosen the hummus.

meals.title: Boiled egg
steps: Boil the eggs for 9–10 minutes until fully set.
Cool, peel and eat with a pinch of salt.
meals.tip: Keep the seasoning light, and skip pepper or chilli if your stomach is sensitive.

meals.title: Peanut butter on apple slices
steps: Core and slice the apple.
Spread or dip the slices in peanut butter.
Add a pinch of cinnamon.
meals.tip: Squeeze a little lemon on the apple to stop it browning.

meals.title: Idli with a little strained moong dal or curd
ingredients: 1/4 cup moong dal, cooked and strained
steps: Steam or warm the idlis until soft.
Cook the moong dal until very soft, mash and strain it into a thin soup.
Serve the idlis with the dal or curd.
meals.tip: Skip the spicy chutney and sambar while your stomach is sensitive.

meals.title: Plain dosa with curd
steps: Cook the dosas thin and soft with very little oil.
Serve warm with a bowl of curd.
meals.tip: Avoid heavy fillings, and keep the dosa pale rather than crispy.

meals.title: Rava/sooji upma with soft-cooked carrot (no peanuts)
ingredients: 1 tsp oil or ghee, mustard seeds, curry leaves
steps: Roast the rava lightly and set aside.
Cook the carrot in a little water until completely soft.
Add the tempering, 1 cup of hot water and salt, then stir in the rava slowly.
Cook for 2 minutes until soft and fluffy.
meals.tip: Skip the peanuts and chilli for a gentler upma.

meals.title: Soft poha with potato and turmeric, with a glass of milk or buttermilk
steps: Cook the diced potato in a little water until soft.
Rinse the poha, drain and add it with turmeric and salt.
Steam gently for 2 minutes until soft.
Serve with milk or buttermilk.
meals.tip: Leave out peanuts, chilli and onion if they trouble you.

meals.title: White toast with smooth peanut butter and ripe banana
steps: Toast the bread lightly.
Spread with smooth peanut butter.
Top with the ripe banana.
meals.tip: Choose smooth, not crunchy, peanut butter.

meals.title: Curd/yoghurt with ripe banana or papaya
ingredients: 1/2 ripe banana or a few pieces of ripe papaya
steps: Spoon the curd into a bowl.
Add the mashed or sliced fruit.
meals.tip: Both banana and papaya are gentle on the stomach.

meals.title: Scrambled or boiled eggs with white toast
steps: Scramble the eggs gently in a little butter on low heat, or boil them for 9–10 minutes.
Season lightly.
Serve with the toast.
meals.tip: Keep the heat low for soft, creamy scrambled eggs.

meals.title: Silken tofu scramble with white toast
steps: Mash the tofu gently with a fork.
Warm it in the oil with turmeric and salt for 3–4 minutes.
Serve on or beside the toast.
meals.tip: Silken tofu is softer and easier to digest than firm tofu.

meals.title: Rice kanji or semolina porridge with milk
ingredients: Pinch of salt or sugar to taste
steps: Simmer the rice in plenty of water until very soft, or stir the semolina into hot milk.
Cook for 5–10 minutes, stirring.
Add a pinch of salt or a little sugar.
meals.tip: Kanji is very soothing when your stomach is upset.

meals.title: Curd rice (thayir sadam) with soft-cooked carrot
ingredients: 1/4 cup grated carrot, cooked until soft
steps: Mash the warm rice lightly.
Mix in the curd and salt.
Stir in the soft carrot and curry leaves.
Rest for 10 minutes before eating.
meals.tip: Use room-temperature curd and cook the rice a little extra for a softer texture.

meals.title: White rice + strained moong dal + cooked lauki sabzi
ingredients: Turmeric, salt, a little ghee or oil, cumin
steps: Cook the dal until completely soft, then strain it into a smooth dal.
Cook the lauki with turmeric and a little water until very soft.
Season the dal with cumin in a little ghee.
Serve with the rice.
meals.tip: Lauki is one of the gentlest vegetables, and it's mostly water.

meals.title: Soft phulka + paneer in mild gravy + cooked pumpkin
ingredients: 1–2 soft phulkas (refined wheat flour if needed)
1 small tomato (peeled), turmeric, a little cream or milk
steps: Simmer the paneer in a mild turmeric-tomato gravy with a splash of milk for 5 minutes.
Steam or boil the pumpkin until soft and lightly mash it.
Make soft phulkas.
Serve together.
meals.tip: Keep the spices mild. Skip chilli and heavy garam masala.

meals.title: Plain pasta with tofu and peeled cooked zucchini in a mild sauce (peeled, seedless tomato)
steps: Cook the pasta until very soft.
Simmer the zucchini and tomato in a little water until soft, then mash into a mild sauce with the olive oil.
Warm the tofu in the sauce.
Toss with the pasta and basil.
meals.tip: Peel the tomato by soaking it in hot water for a minute.

meals.title: Egg curry (mild) + white rice
ingredients: Turmeric, a pinch of coriander powder, 1 tsp oil
steps: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with turmeric until soft, then mash.
Add a cup of water and the halved eggs.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Serve over soft rice.
meals.tip: Leave out chilli and whole spices for a gentler curry.

meals.title: Steamed fish + white rice + mashed potato
ingredients: 120 g white fish fillet (e.g. cod, pomfret)
Lemon, salt, a pinch of turmeric
1 potato, peeled, boiled and mashed with a little butter
steps: Season the fish with lemon, salt and turmeric.
Steam for 8–10 minutes until it flakes easily.
Boil the potato until soft and mash with a little butter.
Serve with the rice.
meals.tip: Check carefully for small bones before eating.

meals.title: Chicken and rice soup
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger in 3 cups of water for 15 minutes.
Add the rice and carrot and cook until very soft.
Shred the chicken back into the soup.
Season lightly and serve warm.
meals.tip: A comforting meal when your stomach is recovering.

meals.title: Soft moong dal khichdi (white rice) with curd
steps: Rinse the rice and dal together.
Pressure-cook with 3 cups of water, turmeric and salt until mushy.
Stir in a little ghee.
Serve warm with curd.
meals.tip: Make it soupier with extra water if you need it very soft.

meals.title: Lauki or pumpkin soup + paneer cubes + white bread
steps: Boil the vegetable in water until very soft.
Blend until completely smooth and season lightly.
Add the paneer cubes to warm through.
Serve with the bread.
meals.tip: Strain the soup if there are any fibres left.

meals.title: Idli or plain dosa with strained dal
ingredients: 1/2 cup moong dal, cooked and strained
steps: Cook the dal until very soft and strain to a thin soup.
Warm the idlis or cook the dosas.
Serve together.
meals.tip: Skip coconut chutney and spicy sambar for now.

meals.title: Mashed potato + steamed tofu + cooked carrot
ingredients: Salt, a little butter or oil
steps: Boil the potato and carrot until very soft.
Steam the tofu for 5 minutes.
Mash the potato with butter and salt.
Serve with the tofu and mashed carrot.
meals.tip: Mash the carrot too for an extra-soft texture.

meals.title: Egg drop soup + soft rice
ingredients: 1.5 cups clear chicken or vegetable broth
steps: Bring the broth to a gentle simmer with the ginger.
Whisk the eggs and stream them in slowly while stirring.
Season lightly.
Serve with the soft rice.
meals.tip: Use homemade or low-salt broth.

meals.title: Steamed or poached fish + rice + cooked carrot
ingredients: 1 carrot, peeled and cooked until very soft
steps: Steam or poach the fish in simmering water for 8–10 minutes.
Boil the carrot until soft.
Serve with the rice and a squeeze of lemon.
meals.tip: Poaching in a little milk makes the fish extra tender.

meals.title: Shredded chicken with soft rice and clear broth
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger in water for 15–20 minutes until cooked through.
Shred it finely.
Serve over the soft rice with some of the clear broth.
meals.tip: Strain the broth so it stays clear and light.

meals.title: Ripe banana
steps: Peel and eat. Choose a banana with brown spots for the easiest digestion.
meals.tip: Bananas are gentle and may help replace lost potassium.

meals.title: Plain curd or buttermilk
ingredients: 1/2 cup plain curd, or 1 cup buttermilk
steps: Stir the curd or whisk the buttermilk with a pinch of salt.
Serve cool, not ice-cold.
meals.tip: Skip the roasted cumin and chilli if they irritate you.

meals.title: Rice crackers or plain crackers
steps: Eat slowly with a few sips of water.
meals.tip: Pick plain, low-fat, low-salt crackers without seeds.

meals.title: Stewed apple (peeled)
steps: Peel, core and chop the apple.
Simmer with the water for 8–10 minutes until very soft.
Mash lightly and add cinnamon if you like.
meals.tip: Cooking breaks down the fibre, so it's easier to digest than raw apple.

meals.title: Boiled egg
steps: Boil the eggs for 9–10 minutes until fully set.
Cool, peel and eat with a pinch of salt.
meals.tip: Keep the seasoning light, and skip pepper or chilli if your stomach is sensitive.

meals.title: Coconut water
steps: Serve cool and sip slowly.
meals.tip: Good for hydration when you're recovering from an upset stomach.

meals.title: Smooth peanut butter on white toast
steps: Toast the bread lightly.
Spread with smooth peanut butter.
meals.tip: Use a thin layer if rich food bothers you.
